newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Suspended chief quits African trade grouping.
newsitem.headline: Suspended chief quits African trade grouping.

text.p: The head of the beleaguered Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (Comesa) said on Tuesday he had resigned from the post he was suspended from three months ago for alleged financial abuse.
"I have resigned as secretary-general of Comesa...My decision to step down has been taken following the recent developments at the secretariat of Comesa," Bingu Wa Mutharika said in a statement.

"I am very happy, however, that the allegations made against me for financial mismanagement or impropriety could not be substantiated. Therefore, I am leaving this organisation with my head high," he added.
The Comesa council of ministers headed by Malawian Commerce and Industry Minister Chakakala Chaziya announced Mutharika's suspension in the Zambian capital Lusaka on January 18.
Chaziya told journalists Mutharika would be investigated over allegations that he abused the grouping's financial resources to make international trips without authority, among other things.
Mutharika denied the allegations and accused the Malawian government of trumping up charges in the mistaken belief that he had presidential ambitions.

"My greatest reward is that Comesa is a reality and is viable. Since taking over its leadership, the volume of intra-Comesa trade rose to nearly $2 billion and has been growing at an annual rate over 10 percent," Mutharika said in his resignation statement.

His suspension came shortly after two members of Comesa, Lesotho and Mozambique, announced plans to pull out of the 20-member grouping, saying they preferred to work within the smaller Southern African Development Community (SADC).
SADC comprises Mauritius, Angola, Lesotho, Swaziland, Zambia, Zimbabwe, Namibia, Mozambique, Tanzania, Malawi, South Africa and Botswana.
All except Botswana and South Africa are also members of Comesa, in addition to Burundi, Comoros, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Kenya, Madagascar, Rwanda, Sudan, Uganda and Zaire.
Mutharika was a leading advocate of a merger of the two regional groupings, widely seen to duplicate efforts.
However Comesa's council said a day after Mutharika's suspension that the two organisations would not merge.
